name: Spinodal Decomposition
desc: Cahn-Hilliard spinodal decomposition — an unstable alloy quenched below its miscibility gap unmixes into two phases that then coarsen for minutes, domains swallowing their neighbours and interfaces straightening, while the conserved mean composition walks the morphology from isolated droplets through a bicontinuous labyrinth to inverted droplets and back; rendered as an etched metallographic section, Nomarski interference relief, two-ink riso, ironbow thermal, or sumi ink.

energy.doc: contrast + colour gain across the two phases and the interfacial rim

scale.doc: magnification into a sub-region of the section — guaranteed visible change

speed.doc: simulation rate — how fast the melt unmixes and coarsens (0.2 still evolves)

density.doc: bias of the conserved mean composition: 0 = minority phase A droplets, 0.5 = bicontinuous labyrinth, 1 = inverted

temp.doc: temperature — thermal fluctuation amplitude + the size of the wandering re-melt spot that keeps coarsening alive

relief.doc: interference/etch relief: how hard the interfaces are lit into pseudo-3D

hue.doc: primary hue — anchors the warm phase; the second phase sits across the ramp

x.doc: horizontal pan of the magnified region

y.doc: vertical pan of the magnified region

style.doc: aesthetic: etched metallographic section / Nomarski DIC relief (light only) / two-ink riso misregistration / ironbow thermal / sumi ink on cream

seed.doc: deterministic seed for the quench fluctuation
